# Historical Decomposition

```{r}
library(ggplot2)
dates_formatted <- as.yearmon(time(x))
dates_formatted <- dates_formatted[(p+1):length(dates_formatted)]
str(dates_formatted)
colors_shock <- rev(c("purple", "yellow",  "blue", "red", "green"))
names <- c("$Q_{elec}$" ,"$P_{elec}$", "IPI",  "$HICP$", "Trend")

theta_0 <- matrix(rnorm(10, 0, 1), ncol=2, nrow= length(colors_shock))
irf_response_test <- as.data.frame(theta_0)
irf_response_test$shock <- rep(names, length.out = length(theta_0[,1]))
irf_response_test$shock <- factor(irf_response_test$shock, levels = names)
# fake plot just to construct the correct legend
dates_formatted <- as.yearmon(time(x))
dates_formatted <- dates_formatted[(p+1):length(dates_formatted)]
# Format to shorter labels (e.g., "May 15", "Jun 15", ...)


plot_legend <- ggplot(data =irf_response_test, aes(x=V1, fill = shock))+
  geom_histogram()+
  theme( legend.direction = "horizontal")+
scale_fill_manual(
  values = colors_shock,
  labels = TeX(names))
# Légende personnalisée (à ajuster selon vos besoins)
custom_legend <- cowplot::get_legend(plot_legend)

```

La différence qui existe entre ma série et la série reconstruite
correspond à l'approximation de la limite des horizons.
Lorsque pour une Cholesky, on calcule de plus en plus d'horizons,
la différence entre les deux courbes se réduit
En plus, il y avait la dérive intuitée par Giovanni.


```{r}
plot_hd_meaned <- function(series){
  
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= as.Date(dates_formatted),
    historical_decomp_matrix[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names
  decomp_tot_data <- decomp_tot_data %>%
    mutate(index = row_number())
  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                             cols = -c(time, index),  names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  
  if (length(colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1]) == length(colors_shock)){
    trend_data <- long_data %>%
  filter(category == "$HICP$") %>%
  mutate(
    category = "Trend",
    value = index *mean_vector[series]
  )

# Combiner avec les autres catégories
  long_data <- bind_rows(long_data, trend_data)
  }
  
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  #long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = names)
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  

  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack", alpha = alpha_chosen) +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_shock)[(length(colors_shock)-(dim(decomp_tot_data)[2]-1)+1):length(colors_shock)],
      labels = TeX(names))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # comparison <- lag(as.vector(vars_demeaned[5:96,series]), 20)
  # comparison[1:20] <- rep(vars_demeaned[4,series], 10)
  
  #y_diff <- vars_demeaned[5:nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 
  y_diff <- vars[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 

   data <- data.frame(
    x = as.Date(dates_formatted),
    ytrend = c(1:T)*mean_vector[series],
    #ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) 
    ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) , # Add mean vector to the test series,
     y_hat = cumsum(y_diff) + c(1:T)*mean_vector[series]

  )
  
  my_plot <- my_plot + 
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytest), linetype = "dashed") +
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y_hat), linetype = "dashed", color='darkred') # Add dashed line+
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytest), linetype = "dashed", color='grey') +
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytrend), linetype = "dashed", color='darkred') 
  return(my_plot)
}



plot_hd_demeaned <- function(series){
  
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= as.Date(dates_formatted),
    historical_decomp_matrix[,series,])
  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names
  decomp_tot_data <- decomp_tot_data %>%
    mutate(index = row_number())
  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                             cols = -c(time, index),  names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  
  
  
    #transform the HICP category
  # long_data <- long_data %>% 
  #   mutate(value = ifelse(category == "$HICP$", value + index*mean_vector[series], value))
  # 
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'colors_shock'
  #long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = names)
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  

  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y = value, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack", alpha = alpha_chosen) +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_shock),#[(length(colors_shock)-(dim(decomp_tot_data)[2]-1)+1):length(colors_shock)],
      labels = TeX(names))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # comparison <- lag(as.vector(vars_demeaned[(p+1):96,series]), 20)
  # comparison[1:20] <- rep(vars_demeaned[4,series], 10)
  
  #y_diff <- vars_demeaned[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 
  y_diff <- vars[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 

  data <- data.frame(
    x = as.Date(dates_formatted),
    ytrend = c(1:T)*mean_vector[series],
    #ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) 
    ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) , # Add mean vector to the test series,
     y_hat = cumsum(y_diff) + c(1:T)*mean_vector[series]

  )
  
  my_plot <- my_plot + 
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), linetype = "dashed")  # Add dashed line+
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytest), linetype = "dashed", color='grey')
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytrend), linetype = "dashed", color='darkred') 
  return(my_plot)
}



plot_hd_inflation_glissante_12 <- function(series){
  
  
  decomp_tot_data <- data.frame(
    time= as.Date(dates_formatted),
    historical_decomp_matrix[,series,])

  # Plot the decomposition
  colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1] <- names
  decomp_tot_data <- decomp_tot_data %>%
    mutate(index = row_number())
  # Reshaper les données en format long pour ggplot2
  long_data <- pivot_longer(decomp_tot_data, 
                             cols = -c(time, index),  names_to = "category",
                            values_to = "value")
  # I find a way to calculate trend only when 
  if (length(colnames(decomp_tot_data)[-1]) == length(colors_shock)){
    trend_data <- long_data %>%
  filter(category == "$HICP$") %>%
  mutate(
    category = "Trend",
    value = mean_vector[series]
  )

# Combiner avec les autres catégories
  long_data <- bind_rows(long_data, trend_data)
  }
  
# Exemple : calcul de la moyenne glissante sur les 12 dernières valeurs
  long_data <- long_data %>%
      group_by(category) %>%
      arrange(category, time) %>%  # assure-toi d'avoir une variable temporelle (ex: `time`)
      mutate(rolling_avg = slide_dbl(value, sum, .before = 11, .complete = TRUE))
  
  
  # S'assurer que 'category' a l'ordre des niveaux correspondant à 'rev(colors_shock)'
  #long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = names)
  long_data$category <- factor(long_data$category, levels = rev(names))
  
  

  # Tracer des barres empilées avec ggplot2
  my_plot <- ggplot()+
    geom_bar(data= long_data, aes(x = time, y =rolling_avg, fill = category),
             stat = "identity", position = "stack", alpha = alpha_chosen) +  # Barres empilées
    scale_fill_manual(
      values = rev(colors_shock)[(length(colors_shock)-(dim(decomp_tot_data)[2]-1)+1):length(colors_shock)],
      labels = TeX(names))+
    #scale_fill_manual(values = c("blue", "red", "green"), labels = c("Supply", "Demand", "Other")) +
    theme_minimal()
  
  # comparison <- lag(as.vector(vars_demeaned[(p+1):96,series]), 20)
  # comparison[1:20] <- rep(vars_demeaned[4,series], 10)
  
  #y_diff <- vars_demeaned[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 
  y_diff <- vars[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series] - reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)] 

  data <- data.frame(
    x = as.Date(dates_formatted),
    y = cumsum(y_diff),
    #ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) 
    ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum) + mean_vector[series]
    #ytrend = + c(1:T)*mean_vector[series]
    )%>%  # assure-toi d'avoir une variable temporelle (ex: `time`)
    mutate(rolling_avg_contrib = slide_dbl(ytest, sum, .before = 11, .complete = TRUE))
  
  my_plot <- my_plot + 
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = y), linetype = "dashed")  # Add dashed line+
    geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = rolling_avg_contrib), linetype = "dashed", color='grey')
    #geom_line(data, mapping = aes(x = x, y = ytrend), linetype = "dashed", color='darkred') 
  return(my_plot)
}



```

```{r}
n <-4
# Apply the function to the sequence 3:10
results <- lapply(c(1:n) , plot_hd_inflation_glissante_12)

#enlever la légende
results <- lapply(results, function(p) p + theme(legend.position = "none"))


# Arrange the plots in a grid
plots_grid <- do.call("grid.arrange", c(results, nrow = 2))

# Combine the grid with the legend
final_plot <- plot_grid(plots_grid, custom_legend, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(1, 0.1))

title <- ggdraw() + 
  draw_label(TeX('Historical Decomposition'), fontface = 'bold', x = 0.5, hjust = 0.5)

# Combine the title and the final plot with legend
final_plot_with_title <- plot_grid(title, final_plot, ncol = 1, rel_heights = c(0.1, 1))

# Display the final plot
print(final_plot_with_title)
```

```{r}
alpha_chosen = 1
n_serie = 4

historical_decomp_matrix <- hd_cholesky[,,]
#ne_hd_compare <- plot_hd(series = n_serie)
alpha_chosen = 0.4

df_chol <- ggplot_build(plot_hd_demeaned(series = n_serie))$data[[1]]  %>%
  filter(fill == "green" | fill == "red") %>%
  mutate(
    Method = "Cholesky",
    fill = case_when(
      fill == "green"  ~ "$Q_{elec}$",
      fill == "red" ~ "$P_{elec}$",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_
    )
  )%>%
  filter(!is.na(fill))

historical_decomp_matrix <- historical_decomp_iv_tibo

data1 <- ggplot_build(plot_hd_demeaned(series = n_serie))$data 

df1 <- data1[[1]] %>% 
  mutate(
    Method = "IV",
    fill = case_when(
      fill == "green"  ~ "$Q_{elec}$",
      fill == "red" ~ "$P_{elec}$",
      TRUE ~ NA_character_  # or another fallback label
    )
  )%>%
  filter(!is.na(fill)) 


# 2. Plot separately but still trigger alpha legend
ne_hd_compare <- ggplot() +
  # Cholesky layer (alpha = 1)
  geom_bar(data = df_chol, aes(x = as.Date(x), y = y, fill = fill, alpha = Method),
           stat = "identity", position = "stack") +
  
  # IV layer (alpha = 0.4)
  geom_bar(data = df1, aes(x = as.Date(x), y = y, fill = fill, alpha = Method),
           stat = "identity", position = "stack") +

  # 3. Manual alpha scale
  scale_alpha_manual(
    values = c("Cholesky" = 1, "IV" = 0.4),
    name = "Identification"
  ) +

  # 4. Manual fill scale with LaTeX labels
  scale_fill_manual(
    values = c( "red", "green"),
    labels = c( expression(P[elec]), expression(Q[elec])),
    name = "Shock"
  ) +

  guides(
    alpha = guide_legend(order = 1),
    fill = guide_legend(order = 2)
  )+
  labs(title = "Comparing HD for HICP",
       x = "Time",
       y = "Contribution") 
ne_hd_compare
```

Describing the summation Error

```{r}
series = 4
data <- data.frame(
  x = dates_formatted,
  y = vars_demeaned[(p+1):nrow(vars_demeaned),series],
  ytest = apply(historical_decomp_matrix[,series ,], 1, sum)
)


ggplot(data, aes(x = x)) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y, color = "Actual")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = ytest, color = "Decomposition")) +
  geom_line(aes(y = y- ytest, color = "Error")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Actual" = "blue", 
                                "Decomposition" = "red",
                                "Error"="black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Decomposition of", series, "using historical data"),
       x = "Date",
       y = "Value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```

Montrer le terme de dérive lorsqu'on fait tourner la VAR sans erreurs


```{r}


ggplot() +
  geom_line(mapping= aes(x= dates_formatted, 
                         y = reconstruct_derive_without_errors_ter[,series][c(-1:-p)], color = "Derive"))+
  geom_line(data=data, mapping=aes(x = x, y = y - ytest, color = "Error")) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("Derive" = "blue", 
                                "Decomposition" = "red",
                                "Error"="black")) +
  theme_minimal() +
  labs(title = paste("Decomposition of", series, "using historical data"),
       x = "Date",
       y = "Value") +
  theme(legend.position = "top")
```
